summary.text: 出 is an old character for going out: early forms are analyzed as a foot (止) above an enclosure (凵 or, in some forms, 囗), depicting a step outward. It is also used for related contexts such as sending something out, but the evidence does not establish a complete chronology of those meanings.

formation.text: The supported analysis is an ideographic compound: a pictorial foot, 止, is shown moving out of an enclosure, 凵 (with 囗 in some oracle-bone forms). Shuowen instead described plants growing upward and emerging; that is an early lexicographic interpretation, not confirmation of the earliest graph.

components.text: 止 is analyzed in early forms as a foot moving outward. It is pictorial within 出; later forms made the original component less recognizable.
凵 represents the enclosure or hollow from which the foot moves. Some oracle-bone forms use 囗 instead; the evidence describes it as an alternative early shape, not a separate sound component.

history.text: Paleographic analyses describe oracle-bone and bronze forms as 止 above 凵, with some oracle-bone forms using 囗. The curated oracle-script image is a modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph; its specimen and exact date are not established here.

A secondary graphic analysis proposes that the parts later joined and that 止 came to resemble 屮 in clerical and regular forms. This proposed change helps explain Shuowen’s plant-growth reading, but the dossier lacks a primary glyph-by-glyph demonstration of the sequence.

uncertainties.text: The sources cite early inscription examples but do not establish a securely dated first token or exact first-use date. Their selected examples also do not determine the relative chronology of all senses.

The dossier offers competing Old Chinese reconstructions for the spoken word or words written 出. Those reconstructions concern pronunciation, not an internal phonetic component, and the rationale and scope of the differing account were not independently assessed here.

senses.period: dating unresolved; attested in oracle-bone examples
senses.text: An oracle-bone example 王出 is cited as a motion use. The exact date of that token is not established in this dossier.

senses.period: dating unresolved; attested in oracle-bone examples
senses.text: An oracle-bone example 勿出兵 shows 出 in a context of sending out troops. The evidence does not establish when this use arose relative to ‘go out’.
Cited bronze examples use 出 in contexts involving paying or issuing cloth and issuing or transmitting commands. Their order and semantic links are not established here.
The dossier records ‘produce’ among the character’s glosses, but does not establish its historical development from an earlier sense.
The dossier records ‘stand’ among the character’s glosses, but does not establish its historical development or chronology.

developments.text: The examples attest both motion and sending-out contexts, but do not establish whether one sense developed from the other or their chronological order.

limitations.text: The selected examples and modern gloss lists do not establish a full semantic chronology or the specific transitions to ‘produce’ and ‘stand’.

overview.text: 出 depicts a foot stepping out of an enclosure. Early inscription examples use it for going out and sending out; the sources do not settle when those related uses developed.

components.text: 止 is the foot: it supplies the moving figure in the picture.
凵 is the enclosure; some early forms use 囗 in this position.

relationships.text: In the early-form analysis, 止 depicts the foot moving outward in 出.
凵 depicts the enclosure in the foot-and-enclosure analysis of 出.
